speaker: Jakob
goal: Get SnapSnipe running and make it yours

issues.title: Fork the repo and run the starter app
issues.body:
1. Click **Fork** on the club repo.
2. Open `notebooks/00_run_app.ipynb` in Colab (use the badge in the README).
3. Put your GitHub username in the first cell and run every cell.
4. Open the `gradio.live` link and upload any photo.

**Done when:** the app shows a guess for your photo. (It already works with zero training — it uses CLIP, a model that understands both images and words.)

issues.title: Pick your 3–5 categories
issues.body:
Edit `config.py` on GitHub (pencil icon) and change `CATEGORIES`.

Tips: pick things that *look* different (pizza vs. salad is easier than two kinds of pasta). Ideas: dining hall food, campus spots, sneakers, dogs on campus.

**Done when:** your app guesses between *your* categories.

issues.title: Vibecode your app's look
issues.body:
Paste `app.py` into an AI assistant and ask it to change things. Prompt ideas:
- "Change the title and description to match my categories"
- "Add a soft theme and an emoji to each label"
- "Add 3 example images people can click"

Re-run the notebook to see your changes.

**Done when:** the app looks like *your* project, not the starter.

issues.title: Start your photo collection (20+ per category)
issues.body:
Take or find at least 20 photos per category. On GitHub go to `data/raw/`, **Add file → Upload files**, and upload into a folder named exactly like the category (e.g. `data/raw/pizza/`).

**Done when:** every category has 20+ photos.

speaker: Clement
goal: Run it like a real software project

issues.title: Set up your project board
issues.body:
On your fork: **Projects → New project → Board**. Make columns `Backlog`, `To do`, `In progress`, `Done`. Turn each of this week's tasks into an Issue and add it to the board.

**Done when:** your board has cards and you've moved at least one to Done.

issues.title: Grow your dataset to 40+ photos per category (via a PR)
issues.body:
Create a branch called `add-photos`, upload the new photos there, then open a Pull Request into your own `main` and merge it. Link the issue in the PR description with `Closes #<issue number>`.

**Done when:** the PR is merged and the issue closed itself.

issues.title: Write a dataset card
issues.body:
Fill in `data/README.md` (template is already there): what each category is, where photos came from, how many, and any weird edge cases. Submit it as a PR.

**Done when:** `data/README.md` is filled in on `main`.

issues.title: Review a friend's PR
issues.body:
Swap fork links with someone at the GM. Leave one helpful comment on one of their PRs (a question, a suggestion, or a 🔥).

**Done when:** you've left a review.

speaker: Diego
goal: Know your data before you train on it

issues.title: Run the data exploration notebook
issues.body:
Open `notebooks/01_explore_data.ipynb` in Colab and run it. It charts photos per category, image sizes, brightness, and shows a sample grid.

**Done when:** you've got the charts for your dataset.

issues.title: Clean up bad photos
issues.body:
Use the notebook's **Problems** section: tiny images, exact duplicates, very dark/bright photos. Delete or replace them on GitHub.

**Done when:** the problems section prints no warnings (or you've decided why a flagged photo is fine).

issues.title: Balance your categories
issues.body:
No category should have more than ~2× the photos of another. Add photos to the small ones (better) or remove from the big ones.

**Done when:** the notebook's balance check passes.

issues.title: Write 3 data insights
issues.body:
Add a `## Dataset insights` section to `data/README.md` with 3 things you noticed (e.g. "most salad photos are from above", "campus-spot photos are all daytime").

**Done when:** 3 insights are on `main`.

speaker: Jakob
goal: Train your own classifier and find its mistakes

issues.title: Train your classifier
issues.body:
Run `notebooks/02_train_model.ipynb`. It turns every photo into 512 numbers with CLIP (that's the *transfer learning* part — reusing a model someone else trained) and then fits a **logistic regression** on those numbers (the classical ML part).

**Done when:** the notebook prints your accuracy.

issues.title: Beat the baseline
issues.body:
The notebook compares 3 models: zero-shot CLIP (no training), k-nearest neighbors, and logistic regression. Put the results table in your README.

**Done when:** your README has a results table.

issues.title: Hunt down your model's mistakes
issues.body:
Look at the confusion matrix and the grid of wrong guesses. For each mistake, write one line on *why* you think it happened (bad photo? two categories look alike? weird angle?).

**Done when:** you've written up every mistake (or your top 5).

issues.title: Fix one mistake, retrain, and save model.joblib
issues.body:
Pick your most common mistake and fix the data (add photos of the confused category, remove mislabeled ones). Retrain, download `model.joblib`, and upload it to the root of your repo.

**Marketing bonus:** write your headline stat like a product launch, e.g. *"SnapSnipe tells a Carrillo burrito from a DLG burrito 92% of the time."*

**Done when:** `model.joblib` is in your repo and the app uses it.

speaker: Clement
goal: Ship it with a link anyone can open

issues.title: Create a Hugging Face Space
issues.body:
Make a free account at huggingface.co → **New Space** → SDK: **Gradio**, hardware: **CPU basic (free)**.

**Done when:** your empty Space exists.

issues.title: Upload your app to the Space
issues.body:
Upload these files from your repo: `app.py`, `config.py`, `model_utils.py`, `requirements.txt`, `model.joblib`. The Space builds automatically (~3–5 min).

**Done when:** the Space shows your app.

issues.title: Test it on your phone and fix any build errors
issues.body:
Open the Space on your phone and snap a real photo. If the build failed, open the **Logs** tab, paste the error into an AI assistant, fix, and re-upload.

**Done when:** a phone photo gets a correct guess.

issues.title: Send the link to 3 friends
issues.body:
Ask them to try to *break* it. Write down every wrong guess in a new issue.

**Done when:** you have feedback from 3 people.

gm: How to Talk About Your Own Project
speaker: Sid

issues.title: Polish your README
issues.body:
Fill in every section of the README's **Showcase** template: problem, live demo link, how it works, results, what you'd do next.

**Done when:** a stranger could understand your project from the README alone.

issues.title: Record a 30-second demo
issues.body:
Screen-record yourself using the app on your phone (one right guess, one funny wrong one). Add it to the README as a GIF or video link.

**Done when:** the demo is in the README.

issues.title: Write your resume bullet and 60-second pitch
issues.body:
Formula: *Built [what] using [tools] that [result with a number].* Example: "Built and deployed an image classifier web app (CLIP + scikit-learn + Gradio) that identifies 4 campus dining dishes with 92% accuracy."

**Done when:** both are in your README's Showcase section.

issues.title: Share it
issues.body:
Present at the GM, post on LinkedIn, or both. Tag the club!

**Done when:** someone outside the club has seen it.
